h: Wild Boar, Verderers and Caves Next Door
p: The Sculpture Trail has been part of the forest since the 1980s, with artworks commissioned to respond to the woodland around them. Some pieces have come and gone over the years as wood and weather do their thing, which keeps the trail feeling fresh for repeat visitors. It's a few miles long all in, so let the little ones set the pace and don't feel you have to see every piece in one go.

A heads-up for dog owners and families: the Forest of Dean is home to wild boar. They usually keep well out of the way, but it's wise to keep dogs close and give any boar you do see plenty of space. Sheep wander freely in parts of the forest too, so drive slowly on the lanes.

Just up the road is the Speech House, where the Verderers' Court has met for centuries to look after the forest's ancient rights; the building is now a hotel. Beechenhurst also connects to the forest's family cycle trail, so cyclists can pedal over and join in.

Allow at least half a day. If the weather turns, Clearwell Caves, near Coleford, takes you underground into old iron mines, while Puzzlewood's moss-covered paths have become famous as a filming location. The Dean Heritage Centre at Soudley fills in the story of the forest's miners and free miners, so you can easily build a long weekend out of this corner of Gloucestershire.
